review_notes: Principal question: how local trust relates to consumer complaint counts. Retain Table 3 Panel A column 6 (fully controlled cross-state GSS trust), Table 3 Panel B column 2 (fully controlled state-year GSS trust), and Table 5 column 1 (fully controlled, full-51-state ancestral-trust proxy). The introduction explicitly presents two geographically varying trust measures (GSS and ancestry-based), and Section 4’s dedicated Tables 3 and 5 estimate the same state-level complaint outcome using those main measures; Table 3’s A/B panels provide the cross-sectional and time-series GSS tests the authors describe in the introduction. Table 5 column 1 is selected over its GSS-only column 2 because it retains all 50 states plus Washington, D.C. The Table 5 proxy is therefore retained as a parallel main measure, while the Wells Fargo shock test in Table 4 and within-bank/city estimates in Table 6 are follow-up identification/robustness analyses. Table 7 estimates the paper’s second, distinct bank-fee governance question and remains outside this complaint-outcome family. No fitted construction regression is required for the selected specifications.
The underlying estimators for Table 3 and Table 5 regressions are not named; the extraction does not assume OLS from linear equations or table form.
Table 3 and Table 5 notes do not identify parenthetical numeric cells. Those values are preserved in result evidence and are not classified as standard errors or test statistics.
descriptive_reason: Table 2 reports complaint-count summaries and 2010/2011 state-level summaries. For the Table 3 state-year model, the 2010/2011 values are linked as components/narrower snapshots rather than as full panel distributions. For the Table 5 full-state model, Banked and PerCapitaInc descriptives are available only for the 35 GSS states, narrower than its 51-state fit.
